title: Friends Who Forever Left Us
text:
Friends who forever

left us,


dear friends forever gone,

outside Time

and outside Space!


For the soul nourished on sorrows,

for the pierced heart, perhaps.
editorial_note: This first-line title variant keeps the same English elegiac fragment used for the matching Poe text.

title: Do You Wish to Be Loved?
text:
Do you wish to be loved? Then do not lose

the course of your heart.

Only what you are must you be,

and what you are not, no.

Thus, in the world, your subtle manner,

your grace, your most beautiful being,

will be the object of endless praise,

and love... a simple duty.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the advice structure of the Spanish variant and its final pause before love as duty.

title: To Miss ***
text:
What do I care if my earthly fate does not

hold within me more than a small

thing of this earth? What do I care if years

of love are forgotten in a moment of hatred?


--


I do not weep in any way because the desolate

are happier than I, little one, but

because I see that you grieve over the fate of this one

who is only a passerby on the earth...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the fragmentary address and the dash break from the Spanish catalog text.

title: To...
text:
The bowers where I see,

in dreams, the most varied

songbirds are lips, and they are

your musical whispered words.


Your eyes, enthroned in heaven,

fall at last desperately,

oh God!, into my funereal mind

like starlight upon a veil.


Oh, your heart... I sigh when I wake

and sleep to dream until daybreak

in the truth that gold can never buy

and in the trifles that it could.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the dream-bower imagery and the contrast between priceless truth and purchasable trifles.
